title: Section 110 — Attempt to commit culpable homicide

content.overview: Section 110 — Attempt to commit culpable homicide. The operative rule is the text of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Cite the BNS section, not the repealed Indian Penal Code, for conduct governed by the BNS. Attempt to commit culpable homicide (old IPC 308). Use this when the intended offence is s. 100/105, not murder. Do not confuse BNS 110 with old IPC 309 (attempt to suicide), which was not re-enacted. BNS restatement of IPC 308. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024. Punishment, ingredients and exceptions are only those the section states. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 110. Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 110 (Attempt to commit culpable homicide)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 110 deals with Attempt to commit culpable homicide. It sits in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Attempt to commit culpable homicide (old IPC 308). Use this when the intended offence is s. 100/105, not murder. Do not confuse BNS 110 with old IPC 309 (attempt to suicide), which was not re-enacted. BNS restatement of IPC 308. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 110 is the rule on “Attempt to commit culpable homicide”. The section provides that whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both

Illustrations. The section itself supplies worked examples. In legal analysis, pick one illustration, restate its facts, and show which ingredient it proves. Illustration (a): A, on grave and sudden provocation, fires a pistol at Z, under such circumstances that if he thereby caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 110. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 100, BNS s. 105, BNS s. 109. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 110 is the complete current-law heading for Attempt to commit culpable homicide. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

enhancement.definition: BNS s. 110 provides that whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes proximate acts committed with the intention or knowledge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, providing proportionate punishment for mitigated homicidal attempts.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 110 (corresponding to IPC s. 308).
Basic tier: Act done with intention/knowledge of culpable homicide — imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.
Hurt tier: If hurt is caused to any person by such act — imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both.

Statutory illustration: A, on grave and sudden provocation, fires a pistol at Z under circumstances that if death ensued it would be culpable homicide not amounting to murder. A is liable under this section.
essentialIngredients: The act was done with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances, that if death were caused, the accused would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
The act went beyond mere preparation.
For enhanced penalty: Hurt was caused to any person by such act.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 110 is the counterpart of Section 109. Where an accused performs an act aimed at causing death or with knowledge of likelihood of death, but the circumstances are such that had death occurred, the offence would NOT have been murder but culpable homicide not amounting to murder (either because the mental state satisfied Section 100 but not Section 101, or because one of the five Exceptions to Section 101 applies), the charge is attempt to commit culpable homicide. The punishment is significantly lower than Section 109: up to three years imprisonment for basic attempt, and up to seven years imprisonment if hurt is caused. The classic illustration is firing a weapon upon grave and sudden provocation (Exception 1) or in a sudden mutual quarrel (Exception 4) where the victim survives.
examples: Teaching example (Provocation attempt): An accused, upon receiving grave and sudden provocation, strikes at the provoker with a heavy stick. The blow misses or causes minor bruising. Had death occurred, it would have been culpable homicide under Exception 1. The accused is liable under s. 110.

Teaching example (Sudden fight with hurt): During a sudden heated altercation without premeditation, an accused stabs an opponent in the arm, causing simple hurt. The case falls under Exception 4; the accused is liable under s. 110 (up to seven years).
distinctions: Section 110 vs Section 109: Section 109 applies when the act if successful would be murder (punishing with 10 years to life); Section 110 applies when the act if successful would be culpable homicide not amounting to murder (punishing with 3 to 7 years).
Section 110 vs Simple Hurt (s. 115): In simple hurt, there is no homicidal intention or knowledge; Section 110 requires the mens rea of culpable homicide.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who fired a pistol at a person during a sudden mutual quarrel in the heat of passion, wounding the person's hand, is liable under s. 109 or s. 110.
Rule: If the act occurred during a sudden fight without premeditation (Exception 4), the homicide if completed would not amount to murder, making the attempt punishable under BNS s. 110.
Application: The fight was sudden, unprovoked by unusual cruelty, and hurt was caused.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 110 and punishable with up to seven years imprisonment.

keyTakeaways: Penalizes attempt to commit culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Applies when circumstances or Section 101 Exceptions mitigate the homicidal attempt.
